`spectra_generalized_shift_5.npz` contains the real A and B arrays exported by
`benchmarks/upstream/prepare_spectra.py` for `SymGEigsShift_5`, from Spectra
revision `db1d5cc3279752ca7ea3e33da44ba2a85e4e4a95` (MPL-2.0).
The exporter and upstream reference use seed 123. This is generated numerical
data, not copied implementation source. The case has n=100, k=10, ncv=20 and
sigma=1.2345. Issue #7 records the original block-iteration convergence failure.
The regression independently computes the dense generalized spectrum and
compares original-equation residuals, B-orthogonality and the invariant subspace.

`spectra_null_start.npz` preserves A and the explicit initial vector from
`Example4_1` at the same Spectra revision and exporter. It is generated numerical
data for the nullspace-start regression in issue #8 (n=100, k=3, ncv=6, LA).

`spectra_transformed_sm.npz` preserves A from `SymEigsShift_17` at the same
revision/exporter (n=10, k=3, ncv=6, sigma=1, SM on the inverse operator).
It guards physical accuracy even when the stricter inverse-operator convergence
count makes the upstream adapter report failure (#13).

`cupy_sm.npz` preserves the real FP64 matrix and start generated by CuPy's
`TestEigshSM` at revision `2316a02d70c7e39d6a7c035529df8358d794256e`
(BSD-3-Clause). It uses `testing.shaped_random` (default seed), the original
0.33 density mask and **elementwise** A*A.T, not a Gram product. The resulting
30-by-30 matrix is indefinite; the original residual gate is 1e-12 after
scaling by the matrix Frobenius norm. These are generated numerical data.

`spectra_sparse_sm.npz` preserves the exact real matrices from `SymEigs_17`,
`SymEigs_22`, and `SymEigs_27` at the same pinned Spectra revision/exporter
(n=10/100/1000, k=3/10/20, ncv=6/20/50). These generated numerical data cover
sparse indefinite matrices with predominantly zero diagonals. Regressions use
the original 100-cycle budget and check the requested spectrum, physical
residual, orthogonality, invariant subspace and full convergence counts.

`spectra_buckling_30.npz` preserves the exact A/B arrays for `SymGEigsShift_30`
from the pinned exporter above (n=100, k=10, ncv=20, sigma=1.2345). The stiffness
metric is SPD; the geometric-stiffness matrix is indefinite. Tests compare
largest buckling-transformed magnitudes, A-orthogonality and original residuals.

`spectra_generalized_matched.npz` preserves exact A/B arrays for
`SymGEigsCholesky_17/22/27` and `SymGEigsShift_45` at that same revision. These
are generated numerical data. The former three exercise sparse indefinite
stiffness with non-diagonal SPD mass at n=10/100/1000; the latter exercises
Cayley selection at n=100, k=10, ncv=20 and sigma=1.2345. Independent dense
references verify the requested invariant subspaces, not residuals alone.

`spectra_hermitian_sparse.npz` preserves the exact complex Hermitian matrices
from `HermEigs_17` and `HermEigs_22` at the same pinned Spectra revision, under
keys `a10` and `a100`. The lower triangle is reflected with conjugation, matching
the upstream self-adjoint operator. These generated numerical data have
n=10/100, k=3/10, ncv=6/20 and sigma=0. The source `test/HermEigs.cpp` SHA256 is
`2f8ddf5a1f05877078114716ebbf58f9270e427ea8bf39765ddccc87516ba27e`.
They guard original residuals, requested spectra and complex orthogonality,
and expose inaccurate unmatched general cuDSS factors of the realified matrix.

`spectra_general_sm.npz` preserves `GenEigs_3/21/27` and
`ComplexEigs_3/21/27` from the same pinned Spectra revision/exporter. These are
generated real/complex nonsymmetric matrices at n=10/100, including all five
numerical failures listed in #12 and the additional small strict-count case.
The source SHA256 values are
`3964877e344b6816d552c106eecf72da13ea39f9a73053b32c4c7a002c4ab89e`
for `test/GenEigs.cpp` and
`1146b5691d6615dcae0646cf4c93b2118fb85791d6c742fd46235df1c93fbae9`
for `test/ComplexEigs.cpp`. Regressions use matched inverse factors and explicit
200-cycle compact / 30-cycle wider budgets, preserving k/ncv, requested SM
selection and original residual bounds. Nonsymmetric eigenvectors are checked
for normalization and requested invariant-space membership, not orthogonality.

`spectra_svd_wide.npz` preserves the real 100-by-1000 `SVD_1` matrix under key
`a`, exported at the same pinned Spectra revision. This is generated numerical
data from `test/SVD.cpp` (SHA256
`53fe3cd06b81050a678830164d7a68e10cd54f7b680a94255c3f49eb6327860a`).
The regression uses the validated augmented-space profile k=5, ncv=20,
tol=1e-12 and at most 300 cycles, retaining the original 1e-9 assertions.
It also checks both SVD equations, leading subspaces, orthogonality and all
three convergence counts on two graph replays, for this matrix and its transpose.
The original ncv=10 strict-count failure remains in the upstream report.

`spectra_shifted_far.npz` preserves exact real matrices from `SymEigsShift_2`
and `SymEigsShift_7`, at the same pinned Spectra revision/exporter (seed 123).
These generated numerical data have n=10/100, k=3/10, original ncv=6/20,
and sigma=1/10. SM on the inverse selects physical eigenvalues farthest from
sigma. The regressions use explicit ncv=8/48 profiles and retain the original
100-cycle budget and accuracy bounds; they do not redefine SM as nearest-shift
selection or claim convergence for the original compact profiles.

`general_projections.npz` contains only the complex 50-by-50 projected matrices
from the final pre-Schur snapshots in `results/counts-direct-trace.json` and
`results/counts-shift-trace.json` (`direct` and `shift` keys). These are generated
numerical data from the pinned Spectra `ComplexEigs_16` and
`GenEigsRealShift_12` problems, after 400 and 30 outer cycles respectively.
They retain the near-converged projected spectra that exposed restart stagnation
in #35, without storing the full original matrices or basis. Array SHA256 values
are `f3cc97999ca0577b8f4c35210ea8049d52830509eb03da61ca098626dd462c33`
and `8876fd837d5edea223c9fac804df091d6235f1362bf17c0c306e6db5eec01d1e`.
The tests check independent eigenvalues, backward residuals, normalization and
nested device-conditional replay; these matrices are not an outer-solver test.
